items.title: [ArchDaily] Architecture as Evidence: Reading the Built Environment Through Forensic Investigation
items.content_html: Architecture is commonly examined through its visible form, materials and spatial organisation. The physical fabric of a building can also retain evidence of events and alterations that are not apparent from its present appearance. Cracks, repairs and structural changes may indicate when and how a building was modified, while photographs and material fragments can provide further evidence about the circumstances surrounding those changes. Forensic investigation examines these traces, using the built environment and its surrounding records to establish how particular events, alterations or failures occurred.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Why Material Lifespan Matters More Than Ever
items.content_html: A material's environmental footprint cannot be fully understood without considering its lifespan. A product with relatively low embodied carbon may require frequent replacement, additional installation resources, and repeated disposal over the life of a building. Conversely, a material with a higher initial impact may offer greater long-term value through its durability, reducing the need for future interventions. From this perspective, longevity goes beyond being a technical characteristic; it becomes an essential component of responsible architectural design.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Sede Ser Headquarters / Atelier 77
items.content_html: The expansion of the Ser Cidadão Headquarters in Santa Cruz, the west zone of Rio de Janeiro, embodies in architecture the commitment of a social organization to human and community development. Since 2002, the organization has been involved in projects related to education, culture, work, and health, promoting opportunities for youth in vulnerable territories. In 2006, it received a donation of a historic mansion, the former residence of doctor and senator Júlio Cesário de Melo, whose legacy of care inspired the very essence of the project: to build spaces that welcome, educate, and transform.

items.title: [ArchDaily] AUA Najarian Center / Storaket Architectural Studio
items.content_html: The Najarian Center is a key facility of the American University of Armenia (AUA), located in Yerevan, near the Sergei Parajanov Museum. Established with the support of K. George and Dr. Carolann Najarian, the center is part of a broader initiative to drive social change in Armenia through education and innovation. It provides spaces and resources for learning, collaboration, and fostering social entrepreneurship. As part of the project, reconstruction work has been carried out on the building, including seismic retrofitting, interior and exterior renovations, and the comprehensive implementation of engineering systems.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Police Station for the People / STUDIO MOTLEY
items.content_html: "Build us a Police Station that people don't find intimidating." This simple, yet unusually perceptive brief from the Additional Commissioner became the starting point for rethinking the conventional police station. Located in Devanahalli, a town on the outskirts of Bangalore with a history spanning over 500 years, the project offered an opportunity to reconsider not just the architecture of a largely neglected building typology, but also the relationship between a public institution and the people it serves.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Lamberth Palace Arches / Tigg + Coll Architects
items.content_html: TiggColl has transformed three previously underutilised Victorian railway arches beneath one of London's busiest railway routes into new spaces for studying, socialising and relaxing, developing a demountable mass-timber system that responds to the unique technical challenges of working beneath an active railway.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Exhibition Artifact / Configuración Visual
items.content_html: The Exhibition Artifact (Artefacto Expositivo) arose from a commission to build a temporary support to exhibit architectural models developed by students of the UNIACC School of Architecture during a celebration of the academic community. In response to this brief, the project proposes to expand the possibilities of the exhibition display, understanding that a structure designed to hold objects can, at the same time, create an environment capable of hosting a collective gathering.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Hotel Tepoztlán / Taller Carlos Marín + Pasquinel Studio
items.content_html: Located between Tepoztlán and Amatlán in the State of Morelos, the Hotel Tepoztlpán designed by the Carlos Marín and Pasquinel Studio Workshop Offices integrates the topography, the landscape and the views of the Tepozteco in a master plan where 4 buildings with different architectural programs explore the virtues of the site. The land was an abandoned plot, where wild vegetation, along with several medium and tall trees were located naturally on the site. From the beginning, this natural condition and respect for the flora of the site was a determining factor for positioning each of the volumes that comprise the project. Another condition that the terrain presents is its rugged topography, the access volume -a staple of pigmented concrete- is located at the foot of the sidewalk, and as we go deeper into the terrain we discover the 4 buildings, the terrain dictated the terrain and program of each of the buildings. The gentle ramps and staircases allow us to reach the pool area, which is -2.5m from the access level, while the room building makes the first forced stop for the user to the center of the land and to an altitude of - 1.20m.

items.content_html: Located on Nuns' Island in Montréal, the Darwin bridges open new architectural perspectives through their use of local sustainable materials.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Hotel Casa Zamná Tulum / Studio Arquitectos
items.content_html: Located on the heavenly beaches of Tulum, Casa Zamná is an architectural project facing the Caribbean Sea. This boutique hotel developed on a 5,160 m² plot and carefully designed by StudioArqs, stands as a tribute to nature and local culture, achieving a harmonious fusion between contemporary design and the most traditional elements of the region.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Snake Building / C+S Architects
items.content_html: The Snake Building in Aarschot, Belgium, is part of a collaboration with a2o Architekten, a Hasselt-based office, commissioned by the client to design the urban regeneration of the De Torens masterplan: a former industrial site in the center of Aarschot, developed with housing, commercial, and public spaces. A series of collegial workshops in Hasselt initiated the design process and assigned the plots to each office (a2o Architekten, C+S Architects, De Vylder Vynck and DRDH).

items.title: Room for Body and Soul: 7 Unbuilt Healthcare Facilities from the ArchDaily Community
items.content_html: Few programs carry as many meanings as healthcare. Depending on the context, health can refer to the treatment of disease, the prevention of illness, physical rehabilitation, or a broader condition of physical, mental, and social well-being. The following projects, shared by ArchDaily readers, offer a specific response to each of these understandings, from hospitals organized around diagnostic and surgical efficiency to centers where sensory regulation, contact with nature or community life sit at the core of care. Together, this group of unbuilt or unfinished projects also offers insight into concepts of health that extend beyond injury or illness toward a more holistic understanding of well-being.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Design Museum Gent / Carmody Groarke + ATAMA + RE-ST
items.content_html: After four years of intensive renovation and expansion, Design Museum Gent will opened its doors close to UNESCO World Heritage sites. What was once a charming but fragmented ensemble of buildings is now a renewed, forward-looking museum that brings together history, innovation and sustainability. The transformation includes both the restoration of listed buildings dating from the 16th to the 20th century and the addition of a striking new wing that gives the museum a fresh, contemporary appearance.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Connecting Old and New Through a Ceramic Facade
items.content_html: Refurbishing an operational industrial complex means working within an architecture shaped by daily activity and circulation. At HTBA (HealthTech Bio Actives), a manufacturer of bioactive ingredients for the pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, and food industries, Martín Lejarraga Oficina de Arquitectura reorganizes and upgrades the industrial facility in Beniel while respecting its production logic.

items.title: [ArchDaily] What Happened to Parametricism? How a Style Blurred Into a Look
items.content_html: In September 2008, at a series of sessions organized alongside the 11th Venice Architecture Biennale under the name of the Dark Side Club, a text was presented that announced, for the first time since Modernism, a new style for architecture. Parametricism as Style, written by Patrik Schumacher, then a partner at Zaha Hadid Architects, called it "the great new style after modernism" and recast Postmodernism and Deconstructivism as "transitional episodes" that had prepared its arrival. What the manifesto proposed was a design logic in which every element of a project, from the urban plan down to the tectonic detail, the interior and the product, would be treated as a variable, so that form could differentiate continuously and adapt to the shifting demands placed upon it.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Architecture as a Social Practice: Lessons from Ammodo Architecture Days
items.content_html: What connects a cooperative housing development in Barcelona, a cultural institution hosted in an unfinished concrete structure in Accra, and a floating festival platform in the Peruvian Amazon? Despite their unique geographic and social contexts, these projects encourage an understanding of architecture that extends beyond the construction of buildings. Through collective housing, adaptive reuse, participatory design processes, and community-led initiatives, they demonstrate how architectural practice creates opportunities for communities to shape their built environments.
